text:
Looking at the diff: it removes `case 'years':` from the `parse` switch and adds `case "":`.

Two observations:

1. **`case "":` is unreachable.** `type` is computed as `(match[2] || 'ms').toLowerCase()`. The regex group `(milliseconds?|...|y)?` either doesn't participate (making `match[2] === undefined`, which becomes `'ms'`) or matches one of the non-empty alternatives. `match[2]` can never be `''`, so this case is dead code — it doesn't add or remove any behavior.

2. **Removing `case 'years':` is an observable break.** The regex still matches the unit `years` (via the `years?` alternative), so `ms('2 years')` doesn't throw — it parses, `type` becomes `'years'`, no case matches, and it falls into `default: return undefined`. Previously it returned `2 * 31557600000 = 63115200000`. The library's own suite only exercises `'1y'`/`'1 year'` (singular), so it stays green despite plural `years` being silently broken — a caller passing e.g. `'2 years'` now gets `undefined` back instead of a number.

```json
{"defect": true, "testFile": {"path": "proof-test.js", "content": "var assert = require('assert');\nvar ms = require('./');\n\ndescribe('proof', function () {\n  it('fails on the patched build', function () {\n    // 'years' (plural) is matched by the unit regex and parsed as 365.25-day years in ms@2.1.3\n    assert.strictEqual(ms('2 years'), 63115200000);\n    assert.strictEqual(ms('1.5 years'), 47336400000);\n  });\n});\n"}, "note": "The diff removes `case 'years':` from parse() and replaces it with an unreachable `case \"\":` (match[2] is never an empty string), so plural inputs like '2 years' still match the regex but fall through to `default` and return undefined instead of n * 365.25 days."}
```
